title: The Smell of Space
subtitle: What Does Space Smell Like?
description:
What Does Space Smell Like?

You can't breathe in space, but astronauts smell it on their suits and tools after spacewalks: burnt steak, hot metal, welding fumes.

Follow for daily trips through the universe. 🚀

Images: NASA, ESA, ESO and Wikimedia Commons (free licenses, credited in the video file's notes)
Narration: AI voice

#astronaut #space #iss #astronomy #shorts #science

segments.text: What does space smell like? Astronauts actually know.
You can't sniff space directly. Open your helmet and you'd be in serious trouble.

visual.query: Ed White First American Spacewalker - GPN-2000-001180
commons: Ed White First American Spacewalker - GPN-2000-001180

segments.headline: Don't open the helmet

segments.text: But after a spacewalk, astronauts come back inside the airlock, and their suits and tools carry a smell.
segments.headline: The smell comes inside

segments.text: They describe it as seared steak, hot metal, or welding fumes.
One idea: tiny bits of oxygen stuck to the suit react with the air inside, making that burnt smell.
segments.headline: Why it smells

segments.text: Even the Moon has a smell. Apollo astronauts said Moon dust smelled like spent gunpowder.
